text:
Elaine: quick q — we keep running into messy auth assumptions when a request flows hosted->dedicated->private sidecar. can we define a minimal credential split so hosted never sees customer data keys and private has a short-lived stepdown token?
Samir: tl;dr yes. propose 2-tier tokens: control-plane token (longer lived, per-tenant, used for routing/quotas) and data-plane ephemeral tokens (minted per-session, scoped to model invocation). hosted only gets control tokens.
Jia: this matches a lot of onprem reqs. question: who mints ephemeral tokens for private? the control plane or the customer's KMS? if control plane mints, we need proof-of-origin.
Elaine: good Q. my thought: control plane issues a signed nonce that private exchange against local KMS to mint data token. private returns an attestation blob we verify.
Pratik: attestation makes ops nervous. alternative: do an asymmetric delegation — control issues a short-lived delegation JWT that references a key ID. private signs and returns a signed receipt. verification = verify signature + check key id in tenant manifest.
Nina: also need rotation rules and auditing. logged receipts should include key fingerprint and operation hash. retention controlled by tenant config.
Samir: agree. also don't cache data-plane tokens in hosted layer. keep them ephemeral in runtime. caching is ok inside the dedicated/private runtime to reduce latency but must honor TTL and revocation.
Elaine: sketching a simple exchange below:
```
# client -> hosted
POST /v1/generate
Auth: Bearer CP_TOKEN
---
# hosted -> control plane
POST /v1/mint-ephemeral
Body: {tenant_id, requested_scope}
Auth: Bearer CP_TOKEN
-> returns {delegation_jwt, expires_at}
# hosted -> private-sidecar
POST /local/mint
Body: {delegation_jwt}
Private checks delegation, uses local KMS to mint DATA_TOKEN, returns {data_token, attestation_sig}
# hosted routes request to private with Data-Token in transport (mTLS + header)
```
Jia: what about offline private (air-gapped)? delegation_jwt should be serializable and redeemable without contacting control plane. maybe use delegation with embedded constraints and short expiry.
Runtime-bot: deploy-canary: pushed adapter-change branch auth-surface-split to staging at 11:08 UTC :rocket:
Pratik: ops note — for canary we should enable strict logging, and a fast rollback circuit if attestation failures > 0.5% over 5m.
Nina: perf note — attestation verification per-request could add ~1ms on x86, but on constrained ARM boxes it's more. consider batching verifications for streaming requests.
Elaine: followups: (1) define fields in delegation_jwt (key_id, scopes, nonce, expiry, issuing_node), (2) spec attestation blob format, (3) add audit sinks for receipts. i'll draft an RFC, want reviews from @samir @jia @pratik.
Samir: ack, will review.
Jia: will help with attestation proto.
Pratik: will outline rollback/circuit breaker thresholds.
Nina: will add retention/PII considerations for receipts.
Elaine: cool — filing RFC now. thanks all :thumbsup:
